title: Aloo paratha
summary: Golden wholewheat flatbreads stuffed with spiced mashed potatoes, crisp outside and soft within.
ingredients: 300 g wholewheat atta flour, plus 1/4 cup extra for rolling
450 g potatoes, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks
method: Mix the atta flour, half the salt and 180 ml water into a soft dough. Knead for 3–4 minutes until smooth, then cover and rest for 20 minutes.
Boil the potatoes in salted water over high heat, then simmer on medium for 12–15 minutes until a knife slides in easily. Drain and steam-dry for 5 minutes.
Mash the potatoes smooth, then mix in the chilli, cumin seeds, garam masala, coriander and remaining salt. Cool for 5 minutes and roll into 6 balls.
Divide the dough into 6 balls. Flatten each, enclose a potato ball, seal well, then roll into an 18 cm round using the extra flour for dusting.
Heat a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat for 2 minutes. Cook each paratha for 1 minute until pale spots appear, then flip and brush with melted butter.
Cook 30–60 seconds each side, brushing the other side with butter, until golden brown with darker spots. Keep wrapped in a tea towel and serve hot.

stages.title: Make and rest the dough
steps: Combine the atta flour and 1/4 tsp of the salt in a large bowl.
Gradually add 180 ml water, mixing with your hand until a soft, shaggy dough forms.
Knead on a bench for 3–4 minutes until smooth and supple, then cover with a damp tea towel.
Rest the dough for 20 minutes, which relaxes the gluten so the parathas roll without tearing.

stages.title: Cook and season the potato filling
steps: Put the potatoes in a saucepan, cover with cold water and add a pinch of salt, then bring to the boil over high heat.
Reduce to medium heat and simmer for 12–15 minutes until a knife slides in easily.
Drain well and leave in the colander for 5 minutes so the steam escapes.
Mash the potatoes until completely smooth, then stir in the chilli, cumin seeds, garam masala, coriander and the remaining 1/4 tsp salt.
Cool the filling for 5 minutes, then roll it into 6 equal balls.

stages.title: Stuff and roll the parathas
steps: Divide the dough into 6 equal portions and roll each into a ball.
Flatten one dough ball into a 9 cm round, using a little of the extra flour for dusting.
Place a potato ball in the centre, pull the edges up around it and pinch together to seal fully.
Flatten the sealed ball gently, then roll with light pressure into an 18 cm round, dusting with flour as needed.
Repeat with the remaining dough and filling, stacking the rolled parathas with baking paper or flour between them.

stages.title: Cook the parathas
steps: Heat a large non-stick frying pan or flat skillet over medium-high heat for 2 minutes until hot.
Cook one paratha for 1 minute, until small bubbles appear and the underside has pale spots, then flip.
Brush the top with some of the melted butter and cook for 1 minute, then flip and brush the other side.
Cook for a further 30–60 seconds each side, pressing gently with a spatula, until both sides are golden brown with darker spots.
Keep the cooked parathas wrapped in a clean tea towel while you cook the rest, then serve hot.

tips: Mash the potatoes until there are no lumps and let them cool; a wet or lumpy filling splits the dough when rolling.
Seal the dough completely around the filling, because any gap lets the potato leak out and burn in the pan.
Dust with only as much flour as needed, since excess flour scorches in the pan and tastes bitter.
Cook over medium-high heat so the parathas brown and cook through quickly; a low heat dries them out and makes them tough.
variations: Add 1/2 tsp ground turmeric and 1/2 tsp chilli flakes to the filling for a more fiery, golden paratha.
Mix 60 g crumbled paneer into the mashed potato for a richer, creamier filling.
storage: Cool completely, then refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 2 days or freeze with baking paper between layers for up to 1 month. Reheat in a dry frying pan over medium heat for 1–2 minutes each side until hot through.

title: Dhokla
summary: Fluffy steamed chickpea cakes topped with mustard seeds, curry leaves and fresh coriander.
method: Sift the chickpea flour into a bowl, then whisk in the yoghurt, 120 ml water, turmeric, salt and half the sugar for 2 minutes until smooth. Rest 10 minutes. Oil a 20 cm cake tin.
Bring 3 cm water to the boil in a wide pot with a rack over high heat, then reduce to medium to keep it steadily simmering.
Whisk the fruit salt into the batter until frothy and paler. Pour into the tin, set on the rack, cover and steam 15–18 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool the dhokla in the tin for 10 minutes, then run a knife around the edge and turn it out onto a board.
Heat the remaining oil in a small pan over medium heat, then cook the mustard seeds until they pop. Add the curry leaves and chilli for 15 seconds.
Add 2 tbsp water and the remaining sugar, simmer 1 minute until dissolved. Spoon over the dhokla squares and scatter with the coriander.

stages.title: Make the batter
steps: Sift the chickpea flour into a large bowl so there are no lumps.
Add the yoghurt, 120 ml water, turmeric, salt and half the sugar.
Whisk for 2 minutes until completely smooth and thick like pancake batter.
Brush a 20 cm round cake tin with 1 tbsp of the oil so the dhokla releases cleanly.

stages.title: Rest the batter and heat the steamer
steps: Cover the bowl and rest the batter for 10 minutes so the flour hydrates.
Meanwhile, pour 3 cm water into a large wide pot with a rack and bring to the boil over high heat.
Lower the heat to medium so the water keeps simmering steadily.

stages.title: Steam the dhokla
steps: Whisk the fruit salt into the rested batter for 10 seconds until it turns frothy and slightly paler.
Pour the batter straight into the greased tin and set it on the rack in the pot.
Cover with a lid and steam over medium heat for 15–18 minutes, until the dhokla is risen and a skewer inserted in the centre comes out clean.

stages.title: Cool the dhokla
steps: Lift the hot tin out carefully and cool for 10 minutes so the cake firms up.
Run a knife around the edge and turn the dhokla out onto a board.

stages.title: Temper and serve
steps: Heat the remaining 2 tbsp oil in a small frying pan over medium heat for 1 minute, then add the mustard seeds and cook until they start to pop, about 30 seconds.
Add the curry leaves and chilli and stir for 15 seconds.
Pour in 2 tbsp water and add the remaining sugar, then simmer for 1 minute until the sugar dissolves.
Cut the dhokla into squares, spoon the tempering over the top and scatter with the coriander.

tips: Add the fruit salt only just before steaming, because it reacts with the yoghurt straight away and the bubbles that make the dhokla light are lost if the batter waits.
Sifting the chickpea flour prevents lumps, which would steam into dense pockets.
Wrapping the pot lid in a clean tea towel stops condensation dripping onto the surface and leaving it soggy.
variations: Stir 2 tbsp finely grated ginger into the batter for a sharper, warmer flavour.
Replace the chilli in the tempering with 1 tsp sesame seeds for a milder, nutty finish.
storage: Refrigerate the dhokla in a covered container for up to 2 days. Reheat in a steamer or microwave for 1–2 minutes until hot, and add the tempering fresh if you can.
